inputs.text: The rally’s scale and its timing weeks before local elections make the “spontaneous” story hard to swallow. Hundreds of groups don’t simply converge around a message by accident; this looks coordinated to keep voters focused on a designated far-right threat while narrowing the range of views treated as acceptable. The anti-extremism language may be less a warning than a tool for steering public opinion. The real question is who benefits from directing attention this way—and what they don’t want voters looking at instead.
